H_hierarchical.evidence: No nested modes or composite states are described; the behavior is a flat arrival-close, crossing-hold, departure-open sequence.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Transitions are mostly simple sensor/timing conditions: first IR closes the gate, second IR opens it; timing is only vaguely said to depend on train speed and length.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: On train detection the controller drives the motor, changes road/train lights, activates the buzzer, updates LCD/status outputs, and controls H-bridge transistor pairs for close/open/stop.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The paper motivates accident avoidance but gives no explicit fault, emergency-stop, rollback, or recovery transition.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Gate close/open behavior is described in the abstract and circuit description, while the actuator-level Q1/Q4, Q2/Q3, all-open motor actions appear later in the Working section.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as level crossing, H-Bridge, buzzer, and light signal are either ordinary component names or are explicitly explained in the paper.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions are not in a state table; the modeler must infer state/action mapping from prose about sensors, lights, buzzer, LCD, motor, and H-bridge behavior.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The paper mentions timing based on train speed and length, but does not specify a concrete arithmetic or boolean guard combining variables.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No parent/composite state is defined, so there is no parent entry/during/exit behavior.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: No from-any-state fault or global recovery rule is described.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain is present.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: No explicit arithmetic/boolean guard set is available for SMT-style consistency checking.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: No global cross-cutting transition over multiple substates or parent during monitor is described.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Outputs are concrete effectors: DC motor, H-bridge transistors, buzzer, light indicators, and LCD display.

key_nl_quotes: The gate is closed, when the train crosses the first IR sensor and the gate is opened, when the train crosses the second IR sensor.
When the transistors Q1 and Q4 are closed, the motor rotates in one direction for closing the railway gate.
one_line_pitch: This is a modest action-heavy railway-gate controller where the main baseline trap is reconstructing scattered prose actions into a coherent flat EFSM.
rationale: The sample has strong transition-action content because one sensing event fans out to motor, warning, light, display, and H-bridge outputs. However, it has no hierarchy, no fault recovery, and only weak guard complexity, so it is not a top stress-test for the weakest Apvrille dimensions beyond actions. Its baseline difficulty comes mainly from scattered prose-to-action attribution rather than from advanced state-machine structure.
